title: Scenario 1 — The Happy Path
subtitle: Everything works perfectly
description: A developer pushes a correct Flask app. All 6 pipeline stages pass and the app deploys to production. This is the ideal CI/CD flow.

files.test_app.py:
import pytest
import app as M


@pytest.fixture
def client():
    M.app.config['TESTING'] = True
    M.tasks.clear()
    M.next_id[0] = 1
    with M.app.test_client() as c:
        yield c


def test_health_returns_200(client):
    r = client.get('/health')
    assert r.status_code == 200


def test_health_status_field(client):
    r = client.get('/health')
    assert r.get_json()['status'] == 'healthy'


def test_create_task_201(client):
    r = client.post('/tasks', json={'title': 'Learn CI/CD'})
    assert r.status_code == 201


def test_missing_title_400(client):
    r = client.post('/tasks', json={})
    assert r.status_code == 400


def test_task_has_id(client):
    r = client.post('/tasks', json={'title': 'Test'})
    assert 'id' in r.get_json()
files.Dockerfile:
FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Copy requirements first (Docker layer caching)
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy application code
COPY . .

EXPOSE 5000

# gunicorn = production WSGI server
# NEVER use app.run() in production
CMD ["gunicorn", "--workers", "4",
     "--bind", "0.0.0.0:5000", "app:app"]
files.ci.yml:
name: Flask CI/CD Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - name: Lint
        run: flake8 app.py --max-line-length=100
      - name: Test
        run: pytest test_app.py -v

  deploy:
    needs: test
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: docker build -t flask-api:latest .
      - name: Deploy to production
        run: |
          docker push myrepo/flask-api:latest
          heroku container:release web

stages.name: Code Commit
stages.learn: A developer writes code and runs git push. GitHub receives the push event and automatically triggers the CI/CD pipeline defined in ci.yml. The pipeline starts a fresh virtual machine for a clean, reproducible environment.

terminal_lines.text: $ git commit -m "feat: add task manager API"
[main a3f1c2b] feat: add task manager API

stages.name: Build — Install Dependencies
stages.learn: GitHub spins up a fresh Ubuntu virtual machine. It installs all packages listed in requirements.txt using pip. If any package fails to install the pipeline stops immediately — broken dependencies never reach production.

terminal_lines.text: Installing collected packages: Flask, gunicorn, pytest

stages.name: Lint — Code Style Check
stages.learn: flake8 scans every line of code for style violations. This enforces team coding standards — consistent indentation, line length, and naming. Even working code can be rejected here. Clean code is easier to maintain and review.

stages.name: Test — Run pytest
stages.learn: pytest runs all 5 test functions automatically. Each test makes a real HTTP call to the Flask app using the built-in test client. If any assertion fails the test is marked FAILED and deployment is blocked. Tests are the safety net of CI/CD.

stages.name: Docker — Build Image
stages.learn: Docker packages your app + Python + all dependencies into one portable image. This image runs identically on any server — your Mac, staging, or production. It solves the classic 'it works on my machine!' problem forever.

stages.name: Deploy — Release to Production
stages.learn: The Docker image is deployed to the production server. A health check hits /health to confirm the new version started correctly. Traffic is only routed to the new version after the health check passes. Congratulations — users see the new feature!

terminal_lines.text: Your image has been successfully pushed.
Releasing image web to flask-task-api... done
>> Users can now access the new version!

stages.name: Code Commit
stages.learn: The developer pushes code with a bug on line 11: the health endpoint returns HTTP 500 instead of 200. The code looks almost correct — this is exactly the kind of mistake humans miss in code review but tests catch every time.

terminal_lines.text: >> Note: Bug on line 11 — returns 500 not 200

stages.name: Build — Install Dependencies
stages.learn: The build stage does NOT check code logic — it only installs packages. The bug is hidden inside a function body, so this stage passes just fine. This is why we need the test stage!

terminal_lines.text: >> BUILD stage: PASSED ✓ (bug not detected yet)

stages.name: Lint — Code Style Check
stages.learn: flake8 checks code style only — indentation, line length, imports. It does NOT execute the code or check return values. The bug (wrong status code) passes linting because 500 is syntactically valid Python.

terminal_lines.text: >> LINT stage: PASSED ✓ (bug still not detected!)
>> Only tests will catch this logic error.

stages.name: Test — Run pytest
stages.learn: pytest actually runs the code and checks what it returns. test_health_returns_200 calls GET /health and asserts the response is 200. The app returns 500 — assertion fails — PIPELINE STOPS. The bug is caught before any user sees it!
stages.fail_message: 2 tests failed — pipeline blocked at TEST stage
stages.fail_learn: This is CI/CD working perfectly! The bug was caught at Stage 4, before Docker build and before deployment. Fix the bug on line 11 of app.py (change 500 to 200), push again, and the pipeline will succeed.

terminal_lines.text: >> Deployment blocked. Bug caught before production!

title: Scenario 5 — Deploy & Auto-Rollback
subtitle: Health check fails — old version restored
description: All pipeline stages pass. The new Docker image deploys. But the health check fails — the server returns 503. The CI/CD system automatically rolls back to the previous working version. Zero downtime for users.

files.test_app.py:
import pytest
import os
os.environ['DATABASE_URL'] = 'sqlite:///test.db'
import app as M


@pytest.fixture
def client():
    M.app.config['TESTING'] = True
    with M.app.test_client() as c:
        yield c


def test_health_ok_with_db(client):
    # Tests pass because DATABASE_URL is set in test env
    r = client.get('/health')
    assert r.status_code == 200


def test_create_task(client):
    r = client.post('/tasks', json={'title': 'Test'})
    assert r.status_code == 201

FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
EXPOSE 5000

files.ci.yml:
name: Flask Pipeline with Rollback

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: sqlite:///test.db
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - name: Lint
        run: flake8 app.py
      - name: Test
        run: pytest test_app.py -v

  deploy:
    needs: test
    steps:
      - name: Deploy new version
        run: docker push && heroku release
      - name: Health check
        run: |
          sleep 10
          curl -f https://app.example.com/health || (
            echo 'Health check FAILED — rolling back!'
            heroku rollback
          )

stages.name: Code Commit
stages.learn: The developer adds a database health check to the /health endpoint. The check reads the DATABASE_URL environment variable. In the test environment this is set, so tests pass. But the production server was never configured with this variable.

terminal_lines.text: $ git commit -m "feat: add DB health check"
[main e5g7h9i] feat: add DB health check

stages.name: Build — Install Dependencies
stages.learn: Dependencies install cleanly. The missing environment variable won't be detected until the app actually starts on the production server.

stages.name: Lint — Code Style Check
stages.learn: Code style is clean. flake8 passes. The environment variable problem is a configuration issue, not a code style issue — linting cannot detect it.

stages.name: Test — Run pytest
stages.learn: Tests pass because line 3 sets DATABASE_URL for the test environment. The health check works in tests. This is a tricky real-world scenario: tests pass but production behaves differently because environment configuration differs.

terminal_lines.text: >> Caution: prod env config not tested!

stages.name: Docker — Build Image
stages.learn: The Docker image builds and pushes successfully. It does not know about the missing environment variable — the image is just the packaged code. Environment variables are injected at runtime by the server.

stages.name: Deploy — Health Check & Rollback
stages.learn: The new container starts on production. The CI/CD system waits 10 seconds then calls /health. The server returns 503 Unhealthy because DATABASE_URL is not set. The system automatically rolls back to the previous version — users experience zero downtime!
stages.fail_message: Health check failed — automatic rollback to v1.0 triggered
stages.fail_learn: This is rollback in action — a safety net after deployment! The fix: set DATABASE_URL as an environment variable on the production server (in Heroku Config Vars, AWS Secrets Manager, etc). Never hardcode secrets in code.

terminal_lines.text: Waiting 10 seconds for app to start...
Users are still on v1.0 — zero downtime!
>> Fix: set DATABASE_URL in production config!
